prediction.description: Peripheral, bilateral ground-glass opacity pattern typical of COVID-19 pneumonia.

findings.name: Mean Intensity
findings.explanation: Average pixel brightness of the radiograph.

findings.name: Lung Opacity
findings.explanation: Fraction of the lung fields showing increased density (consolidation / infiltration).

findings.name: Texture Entropy
findings.explanation: Entropy of the intensity distribution - higher values suggest heterogeneous lung texture.

findings.name: Edge Density
findings.explanation: Density of structural edges - raised with interstitial or focal pathology.

findings.name: Symmetry Score
findings.explanation: Left/right similarity of the lung fields - asymmetry suggests unilateral disease.

findings.name: Hilar Prominence
findings.explanation: Brightness of the hilar regions relative to the lung fields.

findings.name: Apical Opacity
findings.explanation: Increased density in the lung apices - typical of tuberculosis reactivation.

findings.name: Peripheral Infiltration
findings.explanation: Peripheral / lower-zone opacity - characteristic of COVID-19 pneumonia.

findings.name: Costophrenic Blunting
findings.explanation: Density at the costophrenic angles - indicates pleural effusion.

findings.name: Image Quality
findings.explanation: Technical quality of the radiograph (sharpness and contrast).

explainability.summary: The prediction 'COVID19' was driven mainly by Hilar Prominence, Symmetry Score, Peripheral Infiltration. The model assigned 52.9% confidence to this class.

recommendations: Peripheral bilateral opacities are compatible with COVID-19 pneumonia - confirm with PCR/antigen testing.
Correlate with oxygen saturation and clinical severity; consider repeat imaging if deterioration occurs.
Marked left/right asymmetry - review for technical rotation before acting on the findings.
A radiologist must confirm every finding reported by this decision-support tool.
